ITQAN:v2p415/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p415/r10.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p415/r10.claim: Dhikr can mean honor or renown.

DAMGHANI:v1p180/r7.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p180/r7.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p180/r7.claim: Dhikr can mean honor or renown for a people.
DAMGHANI:v1p180/r7.anchor: السابع : الذكر بمعنى الشرف قوله تعالى في سورة الزخرف

QURTUBI-FULL:76:1/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:76:1/r9.speaker: القشيري
QURTUBI-FULL:76:1/r9.claim: Another interpretation takes remembrance as rank and honor, which Adam gained when God made him a vicegerent and entrusted him with what the heavens and mountains declined.
QURTUBI-FULL:76:1/r9.anchor: بل هذا الذكر بمعنى الخطر والشرف والقدر

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:40/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:40/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:40/r1.claim: People hardened by conditioning may lose the ability to hear, see, and think rightly, making rational persuasion nearly impossible.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:40/r1.anchor: Şartlanmışlık sebebiyle doğruyu dinleme, görme ve doğru düşünme kabiliyetlerini kaybetmiş kimselere laf anlatmak imkânsız gibidir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:40/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:40/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:40/r2.claim: The Prophet and those continuing his preaching should be patient and leave matters to God instead of despairing that people ignore them or that wrongdoers’ punishment is delayed.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:40/r2.anchor: Hz. Peygamber’in ve onun tebliğ sünnetini yerine getiren ümmetin, “Neden bizi dinlemiyor ve anlamıyorlar?” veya “Bunca zulme ve sapkın inançlarda ısrara rağmen niçin bunlara hak ettikleri ceza verilmiyor?” sorularıyla bunalmamaları, aksine sabretmeleri, işi Allah’a bırakmaları gerekmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:40/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:40/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:40/r3.claim: Whether or not God shows the Prophet the polytheists’ fate, He will act as required and repay everyone; no power can withstand Him.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:43:40/r3.anchor: Allah, Hz. Peygamber’e müşriklerin âkıbetini gösterse de (nitekim bir kısmını Medine döneminde göstermiştir) göstermese de gerekeni yapacak, herkese hak ettiğini verecektir

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p170/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p170/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p170/r4.claim: The rejecters' rebellion stems from affluence, which cannot outweigh the Hereafter; Satan's blindfold will lift too late, so the Prophet must persist in preaching the true religion attested by all prophets.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p170/r4.anchor: The real thing which has become a source of trial for them is their affluence even though this affluence cannot tilt the scales of God’s balance

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r4.claim: Every part of Sūrah al-Zukhruf relates deeply to its central theme, and the whole sūrah forms a harmonious unit from beginning to end.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r4.anchor: each part of it is deeply related to its central theme

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p184/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p184/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p184/r4.claim: After the historical example, the passage highlights Quraysh's real rebelliousness and assures the Prophet to persist: he calls to the messengers' true path, while God may judge opponents but grants them respite by His established practice.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p184/r4.anchor: the Prophet (sws) is assured that he should adhere to his preaching

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p194/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p194/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p194/r5.claim: The Qur'an is a reminder for the Prophet and his nation, and every person will be questioned about it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p194/r5.anchor: is a reminder for him as well as for his nation, and one day each person

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p195/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p195/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p195/r1.claim: Messengers answer for faithfully delivering revelation and their people's response; nations answer for their conduct despite receiving a warner, as 7:6-7 describes.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p195/r1.anchor: The accountability of the nation will be about what they have done in spite of the coming of a warner to them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p195/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p195/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p195/r2.claim: The final accounting rewards messengers and their companions and punishes rejecters; this assures Muhammad and his companions and threatens his opponents with God's final judgment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p195/r2.anchor: one day, the whole case will be presented in the court of God and there one will come to know who won and who lost.

BURSEVI:v8p286#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p286#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p286#2/r4.claim: The Qur’an is a great honor especially for the Prophet and generally for his community; a Prophetic report says every thing boasts of its distinction and the community’s distinction is the Qur’an.
BURSEVI:v8p286#2/r4.anchor: كما قال عليه السلام : إن لكل شيء شرفا يباهي به وإن بها أمتي وشرفها : القرآن.

BURSEVI:v8p286#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p286#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
BURSEVI:v8p286#2/r5.claim: Mujāhid says “your people” means the Muslim community.
BURSEVI:v8p286#2/r5.anchor: فالمراد بالقوم : الأمة. كما قال مجاهد ،

BURSEVI:v8p286#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p286#2/r6.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v8p286#2/r6.claim: Another view takes “your people” to mean Quraysh, since people can say the great Book was sent down to one of them.
BURSEVI:v8p286#2/r6.anchor: وقال بعضهم : ولقوتك من قريش حيث يقال : إن هذا الكتاب العظيم إنزال الله على رجل من هؤلاء.

BURSEVI:v8p286#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p286#2/r7.speaker: الكواشي
BURSEVI:v8p286#2/r7.claim: Al-Kawāshī says those nearest to the Prophet have the strongest claim to this honor, beginning with Quraysh, then Banū Hāshim and Banū al-Muṭṭalib.
BURSEVI:v8p286#2/r7.anchor: قال في "الكواشي" : أولاهم بذلك الشرف الأقرب ، فالأقرب منه عليه السلام كقريش

BURSEVI:v8p286#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p286#2/r8.speaker: ابن عطاء
BURSEVI:v8p286#2/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ says the Prophet is honored through affiliation with God, and his people are honored through affiliation with him.
BURSEVI:v8p286#2/r8.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : شرف لك بانتسابك إلينا وشرف لقومك بانتسابهم إليك

BURSEVI:v8p286#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p286#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p286#2/r9.claim: On Judgment Day the community will be asked about the Qur’an, fulfilling its rights, honoring it, and giving thanks for receiving it above other peoples.
BURSEVI:v8p286#2/r9.anchor: يوم القيامة عنه ، وعن قيامكم بحقوقه وعن تعظيمكم وشكركم على أن رزقتموه

BURSEVI:v8p286#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p286#2/r10.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v8p286#2/r10.claim: The inward reading says the Qur’an gives the Prophet and his followers the honor of reaching God; they will be asked whether they fulfilled that honor or misused it for worldly and ego-driven aims.
BURSEVI:v8p286#2/r10.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : وأن القرآن به شرف الوصول لك ولمتابعيك ، وسوف تسألون

BURSEVI:v8p286#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p286#2/r11.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v8p286#2/r11.claim: Another view contrasts gnostic knowledge, grounded in unveiling and vision and ending in God’s presence, with other people’s intellectual learning, worldly posts, and transient goods.
BURSEVI:v8p286#2/r11.anchor: قال بعضهم : علوم العارفين مبنية على الكشف والعيان ، وعلوم غيرهم من الخواطر الفكرية والأذهان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p376/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p376/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p376/r1.claim: The revelation is an honor for the Prophet and his people because it came among them and in their language, making them its recipients.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p376/r1.anchor: أي شرف، حيث نزل عليهم وبلسانهم، جعل تبعا لهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p376/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p376/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p376/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatada, al-Suddi, and Ibn Zayd identify the people as Quraysh and then the Arabs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p376/r2.anchor: القوم على هذا قريش ثم العرب، قاله ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة والسدي وابن زيد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p376/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p376/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p376/r3.claim: A report says the Prophet presented himself to tribes and stayed silent when asked who would rule after him until this verse came; then he answered, “Quraysh.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p376/r3.anchor: فكان إذا سئل عن ذلك قال: «لقريش»

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p376/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p376/r4.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p376/r4.claim: Hasan takes “your people” to mean the Prophet's community and the remembrance as an admonition.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p376/r4.anchor: وقال الحسن: القوم هنا أمته، والمعنى: وإنه لتذكرة وموعظة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p376/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p376/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p376/r5.claim: The verse shows that people may desire honorable praise; God would not have bestowed remembrance on the Prophet if it were not desirable.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p376/r5.anchor: قيل: وهذه الآية تدل على أن الإنسان يرغب في الثناء الحسن الجميل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p376/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p376/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p376/r6.claim: Abraham's prayer for an enduring good name is another example of seeking worthy remembrance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p376/r6.anchor: واجعل لي لسان صدق في الآخرين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p376/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p376/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p376/r7.claim: Good remembrance rivals or surpasses life: life's effect reaches only the living, while a good name endures everywhere and in every age.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p376/r7.anchor: والذكر الجميل قائم مقام الحياة، بل هو أفضل من الحياة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p376/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p376/r8.speaker: ابن دريد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p376/r8.claim: Ibn Duraid's verse supports the value of leaving a good report behind.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p376/r8.anchor: وقال ابن دريد: وإنما المراد حديث بعده

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p376/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p376/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p376/r9.claim: A second poet likewise says that the world's finest qualities are the good reports that remain.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p376/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p376/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p376/r10.claim: Hulagu illustrated enduring remembrance by saying that Muhammad, dead for over six hundred years, was still named from minarets five times daily.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p376/r10.anchor: هذا الذي له أزيد من ستمائة سنة، قد مات وهو يذكر على المآذن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p376/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p376/r11.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p376/r11.claim: Hasan says people will be questioned about gratitude for this blessing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p376/r11.anchor: قال الحسن عن شكر هذه النعمة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p376/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p376/r12.speaker: مقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p376/r12.claim: Muqatil says those who denied the revelation will be questioned in rebuke.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p376/r12.anchor: وقال مقاتل: المراد من كذب به يسأل سؤال توبيخ

QUSHAYRI:v3p177/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p177/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p177/r2.claim: The Qur'an is a remembrance for Muhammad and his people: a source of honor, good reputation, and an entitled rank; they will be questioned about it.
QUSHAYRI:v3p177/r2.anchor: أي إن هذا القرآن لذكر لك ؛ أي شرف لك ، وحسن صيت ، واستحقاق منزلة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p215/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p215/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p215/r2.claim: The Qur’an is an honor for the Prophet and his Qurayshi people; 21:10 similarly calls the revealed Book a reminder or honor for its addressees.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p215/r2.anchor: وإنه} يعني القرآن، {لذكر لك} لشرف لك، {ولقومك} من قريش، نظيره: "لقد أنزلنا إليكم كتابا فيه ذكركم"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p215/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p215/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p215/r3.claim: The Prophet and his people will be asked about the Qur’an’s due and about fulfilling gratitude for it.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p215/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p215/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p215/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak reports Ibn Abbas’s account that the Prophet did not identify who would hold authority after him until this verse came; afterward he answered that it was Quraysh.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p215/r4.anchor: روى الضحاك عن ابن عباس أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا سئل لمن هذا الأمر بعدك؟ لم يخبر بشيء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p215/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p215/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p215/r5.claim: Ibn Umar reports the Prophet saying authority would remain among Quraysh as long as two people remained.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p215/r5.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لا يزال هذا الأمر في قريش ما بقي اثنان"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p215/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p215/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p215/r6.claim: Muʿawiya reports hearing the Prophet say authority is in Quraysh and that God casts down anyone who opposes them while they uphold the religion.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p215/r6.anchor: عن معاوية قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "إن هذا الأمر في قريش لا يعاديهم أحد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p215/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p215/r7.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p215/r7.claim: Mujahid says the Qur’an honors the Arabs because it was revealed in their language, with the greatest share of that honor belonging to Quraysh and Banu Hashim.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p215/r7.anchor: وقال مجاهد: القوم هم العرب، فالقرآن لهم شرف إذ نزل بلغتهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p215/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p215/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p215/r8.claim: Another interpretation says the Qur’an honors the Prophet through the wisdom given him and honors the believers among his people through their guidance.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p215/r8.anchor: وقيل: "ذكر ذلك": شرف لك بما أعطاك من الحكمة

BAYDAWI-FULL:43:41-45/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:41-45/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:41-45/r7.claim: The revelation is an honor for the Prophet and his people, who will be asked about it and their fulfillment of its due.
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:41-45/r7.anchor: لشرف لك. { ولقومك وسوف تسئلون } أي عنه يوم القيامة وعن قيامكم بحقه

BIQAI-FULL:v7p31/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p31/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p31/r4.claim: The revelation is great honor, admonition, and explanation; calling honor dhikr points to remembrance and observance of its law as the source of that honor.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p31/r4.anchor: عبر عن الشرف بالذكر للتنبيه على أن سببه الإقبال على الذكر

BIQAI-FULL:v7p31/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p31/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p31/r5.claim: The Qur'an honors Quraysh, the Arabs, and all its followers because it came through one of them in their language and gives them knowledge, distinction, and leadership.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p31/r5.anchor: قريش خصوصا والعرب عموما وسائر من اتبعك ولو كان من غيرهم

BIQAI-FULL:v7p31/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p31/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v7p31/r6.claim: The Prophet says this leadership remains with Quraysh while two people remain, provided they uphold the religion; those who uphold it are honored in heaven and earth.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p31/r6.anchor: قال صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( لا يزال هذا الأمر في قريش ما بقي في الناس اثنان ما أقاموا الدين )

BIQAI-FULL:v7p31/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p31/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
BIQAI-FULL:v7p31/r7.claim: Ibn al-Jawzi reports al-Daḥḥāk from Ibn ʿAbbās: Muhammad did not name his successor when asked until this verse came, then answered that it would be Quraysh.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p31/r7.anchor: روى الضحاك عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا سئل

BIQAI-FULL:v7p31/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p31/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p31/r8.claim: Biqāʿī infers from that report that Muhammad understood Quraysh would inherit Muslim rule after him through the honor of the Qur'an revealed to one of them.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p31/r8.anchor: وهذا يدل على أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فهم من هذا أنه يلي على المسلمين بحكم النبوة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p31/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p31/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p31/r9.claim: The community will become a source of knowledge for people everywhere about religious and worldly concerns, despite once being regarded as weak and ignorant; it will also be questioned about its duties and response to revelation.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p31/r9.anchor: أي تصيرون في سائر أنواع العلم محط رحال السائلين

DURR-FULL:v7p379/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p379/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p379/r8.claim: The reminder and honor for the Prophet and his people is the Qur'an.
DURR-FULL:v7p379/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما {وإنه لذكر لك ولقومك} قال: القرآن شرف لك ولقومك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p220/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p220/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p220/r5.claim: The Qurʾān is praise and benefit, honoring the Messenger and his people; its followers gain guidance and benefit, while those who reject it are threatened with questioning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p220/r5.anchor: من إرادة أن هذا الدين يكسبه ويكسب قومه حسن السمعة في الأمم فمن اتبعه نال حظه من ذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p220/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p220/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p220/r6.claim: The word dhikr may mean intellectual recollection: guidance to what one did not know, like recalling something forgotten; many explain it as admonition.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p220/r6.anchor: فشبه بتذكر الشيء المنسي وهو ما فسر به كثير الذكر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p220/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p220/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p220/r7.claim: Alternatively, dhikr means public mention: this religion gives the Messenger and his people an honored reputation among nations.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p220/r7.anchor: والذكر بهذا المعنى غالب في الذكر بخبره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p220/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p220/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p220/r8.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr compares the verse’s ten meanings in a line’s space with Imruʾ al-Qays’s celebrated concise line, which has six; the verse adds emphasis, allusion, and verbal ornament.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p220/r8.anchor: قفا نبكك من ذكرى حبيبب ومنزل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p57/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p57/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة ومجاهد والسدي وابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p57/r3.claim: They understand the Qur'an as the Prophet's honor and praise in this world, with “his people” meaning Quraysh and then the Arabs.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p57/r3.anchor: وهذا قول ابن عباس وقتادة ومجاهد والسدي وابن زيد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p57/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p57/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p57/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās recounts that tribes asked who would lead after the Prophet; after this verse was revealed, he said Quraysh, and the Arabs accepted only when the Anṣār did.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p57/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يعرض نفسه على القبائل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p57/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p57/r5.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p57/r5.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports the Prophet saying authority will remain among Quraysh as long as two of them remain.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p57/r5.anchor: وروي عن ابن عمر أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «لا يزال الأمر في قريش ما بقي منهم اثنان»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p57/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p57/r6.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p57/r6.claim: Abū Mūsā reports the Prophet saying authority remains among Quraysh while they judge fairly, show mercy, and honor covenants; whoever fails is cursed by God, angels, and all people.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p57/r6.anchor: وروى أبو موسى الأشعري عنه صلى الله عليه وسلم: «لا يزال الأمر في قريش ما زالوا، إذا حكوا عدلوا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p57/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p57/r7.speaker: معاوية
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p57/r7.claim: Muʿāwiya reports the Prophet saying this authority remains among Quraysh while they uphold the religion.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p57/r7.anchor: وروى معاوية أنه عليه السلام قال: «لا يزال هذا الأمر في قريش ما أقاموا الدين»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p57/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p57/r8.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p57/r8.claim: Al-Ḥasan instead takes “reminder” literally as admonition and “his people” as the entire community.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p57/r8.anchor: ويحتمل أن يريد وإنه لتذكرة وموعظة، ف «القوم» على هذا أمة بأجمعها، وهذا قول الحسن بن أبي الحسن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p57/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p57/r9.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p57/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and others say people will be questioned about the Qur'an's commands and prohibitions.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p57/r9.anchor: قال ابن عباس وغيره معناه: عن أوامر القرآن ونواهيه:

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p57/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p57/r10.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p57/r10.claim: Al-Ḥasan says people will be questioned about gratitude for the blessing of the Qur'an; the wording can encompass both interpretations.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p57/r10.anchor: وقال الحسن بن أبي الحسن معناه: عن شكر النعمة فيه، واللفظ يحتمل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p228#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p228#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة والسدي وابن زيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p228#2/r6.claim: They explain the Qur’an as an honor for the Prophet and his people; Ibn Jarir prefers this meaning and cites no other.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p228#2/r6.anchor: قاله ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وقتادة، والسدي، وابن زيد.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p228#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p228#2/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p228#2/r7.claim: A report from Muawiya says leadership remains among Quraysh, and anyone who contests it while they uphold religion will be cast down; al-Bukhari records it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p228#2/r7.anchor: إن هذا الأمر في قريش لا ينازعهم فيه أحد إلا أكبه الله على وجهه ما أقاموا الدين

NAHHAS:v4p110/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p110/r9.speaker: علي بن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v4p110/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Qur'an is an honor for the Prophet and his people.
NAHHAS:v4p110/r9.anchor: روى علي بن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس قال أن القرآن لشرف لك ولقومك

NAHHAS:v4p110/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p110/r10.speaker: مجاهد
NAHHAS:v4p110/r10.claim: Mujahid interprets the honor as belonging to Quraysh, explaining that when asked one's Arab lineage a Qurayshi answers that he is from Quraysh.
NAHHAS:v4p110/r10.anchor: وتأول هذا مجاهد على أنه شرف لقريش قال يقال ممن الرجل فيقال من العرب فيقال من أي العرب فيقول من قريش

NAHHAS:v4p110/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p110/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p110/r11.claim: Another view says the Prophet's people are those who believed in him and followed his way; another takes the revelation to him and earlier prophets as a reminder to teach religion.
NAHHAS:v4p110/r11.anchor: وقال غيره قومه ههنا من آمن به وكان على منهاجه

QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44/r2.claim: The Quran is an honor for the Prophet and Quraysh because it was revealed in their language to a man from them; other language communities depend on knowing Arabic to understand it, and are thereby honored above other language communities.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44/r2.anchor: يعني القرآن شرف لك ولقومك من قريش، إذ نزل بلغتهم وعلى رجل منهم

QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44/r3.claim: The phrase is linked to the verse saying a Book was sent down to them in which their honor lies.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44/r3.anchor: نظيره: لقد أنزلنآ إليكم كتابا فيه ذكركم

QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44/r4.claim: Other interpretations take dhikr as clarification of what the Prophet and community need, or as a reminder by which they recall religion and act upon it.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44/r4.anchor: وقيل: بيان لك ولأمتك فيما بكم إليه حاجة. وقيل: تذكرة تذكرون به أمر الدين وتعملون به.

QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44/r5.claim: Another interpretation is that dhikr means the caliphate, which belongs to Quraysh; a Prophetic report says people follow Quraysh in this affair, believer after believer and unbeliever after unbeliever.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44/r5.anchor: وقيل: «وإنه لذكر لك ولقومك» يعني الخلافة فإنها في قريش لا تكون في غيرهم قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44/r6.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44/r6.claim: Malik is reported to understand the distinction of Quraysh as the inherited practice of a man saying, “My father told me from his father.”
QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44/r6.anchor: وقال مالك: هو قول الرجل حدثني أبي عن أبيه

QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44/r7.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44/r7.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says that Baghdad's Banu Tamim uniquely preserved this chain of ancestral transmission in Islam, which elevated their status and made people reckon them with the caliphate; he gives the example of two descendants recounting Ali's definition of al-hannan and al-mannan.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44/r7.anchor: قال ابن العربي: ولم أجد في الإسلام هذه المرتبة لأحد إلا ببغداد فإن بني التميمي بها يقولون: حدثني أبي قال حدثني أبي

QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44/r8.claim: The author says the strongest reading is that the phrase refers to the Quran, since the discourse is built on that reading and returns to it.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44/r8.anchor: والأقوى أن يكون المراد بقوله: { وإنه لذكر لك ولقومك } يعني القرآن فعليه انبنى الكلام وإليه يرجع المصير

QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44/r9.speaker: قتادة والحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44/r9.claim: Al-Mawardi records one view that “your people” means those of the Prophet's community who follow him.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44/r9.anchor: أحدهما من اتبعك من أمتك قاله قتادة وذكره الثعلبي عن الحسن.

QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44/r10.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44/r10.claim: Mujahid says “your people” means Quraysh: if asked where someone is from, one says Arabs, then Quraysh.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44/r10.anchor: الثاني لقومك من قريش فيقال ممن هذا؟ فيقال من العرب، فيقال من أي العرب؟ فيقال من قريش قاله مجاهد.

QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44/r11.claim: The author says the Quran honors anyone who acts upon it, whether Qurayshi or not.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44/r11.anchor: قلت والصحيح أنه شرف لمن عمل به، كان من قريش أو من غيرهم.

QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44#2/r1.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44#2/r1.claim: The Prophet tells Fatima, his wives, and his kin to seek salvation from God since he cannot save them from Him; he then denies special standing to Banu Hashim, Quraysh, Ansar, and freedmen, making piety the sole distinction among people descended from one man and woman.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44#2/r1.anchor: أقبل نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من سرية أو غزاة فدعا فاطمة فقال: «يا فاطمة اشتري نفسك من الله فإني لا أغني عنك من الله شيئا»

QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44#2/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44#2/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra transmits a warning against boasting of ancestors: all people are Adam's children, God removed pre-Islamic pride, and people are either pious believers or wretched sinners.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44#2/r2.anchor: " لينتهين أقوام يفتخرون بفحم من فحم جهنم أو يكونون شرا عند الله من الجعلان التي تدفع النتن بأنفها

QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44#2/r3.claim: The author points to a fuller discussion of this theme in the chapter of al-Hujurat.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44#2/r3.anchor: وسيأتي لهذا مزيد بيان في الحجرات إن شاء الله تعالى.

QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44#2/r4.speaker: مقاتل والفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44#2/r4.claim: Muqatil and al-Farra say people will be asked about their gratitude for the Quran.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44#2/r4.anchor: أي عن الشكر عليه قاله مقاتل والفراء.

QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44#2/r5.speaker: ابن جريج
QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44#2/r5.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the Prophet and those with him will be asked about what was brought to them.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44#2/r5.anchor: وقال ابن جريج: أي تسألون أنت ومن معك على ما أتاك.

QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44#2/r6.claim: A further explanation is that they will be asked what they did with the Quran; the interpretations have nearly the same sense.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:43-44#2/r6.anchor: وقيل: تسألون عما عملتم فيه والمعنى متقارب.

TABATABAI:43:41-45/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:43:41-45/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:43:41-45/r5.claim: The apparent meaning of dhikr is remembrance of God, as elsewhere in this sūrah; the lām marks the obligations addressed to the Prophet and his people, and “you will be asked” supports accountability for them on Judgment Day.
TABATABAI:43:41-45/r5.anchor: الظاهر أن المراد بالذكر ذكر الله، وبهذا المعنى تكرر مرارا في السورة، واللام في { لك ولقومك } للاختصاص بمعنى توجه ما فيه من التكاليف إليهم

TABATABAI:43:41-45/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:43:41-45/r6.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
TABATABAI:43:41-45/r6.claim: Most commentators instead understand dhikr as honor or renown: the Qurʾān is a great distinction by which the Prophet and his Arab people are remembered among nations.
TABATABAI:43:41-45/r6.anchor: وعن أكثر المفسرين أن المراد بالذكر الشرف الذي يذكر به، والمعنى وإنه لشرف عظيم لك ولقومك من العرب تذكرون به بين الأمم.

TABRISI:43:41-44/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:43:41-44/r10.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي
TABRISI:43:41-44/r10.claim: The revealed Qurʾan is an honor for the Prophet and his Quraysh people.
TABRISI:43:41-44/r10.anchor: أي وإن القرآن الذي أوحي إليك لشرف لك ولقومك من قريش عن ابن عباس والسدي

TABRISI:43:41-44/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:43:41-44/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:43:41-44/r11.claim: Alternatively, his people are the Arabs because the Qurʾan came in their language; the honor applies especially to Arabs, more to Quraysh, and most to Banū Hāshim.
TABRISI:43:41-44/r11.anchor: وقيل: لقومك أي للعرب لأن القرآن نزل بلغتهم ثم يختص بذلك الشرف الأخص من العرب

TABRISI:43:41-44/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:43:41-44/r12.speaker: الكلبي والزجاج وغيرهما
TABRISI:43:41-44/r12.claim: Being asked means being asked to give thanks for the honor God bestowed.
TABRISI:43:41-44/r12.anchor: عن شكر ما جعله الله لكم من الشرف عن الكلبي والزجاج وغيرهما

TABRISI:43:41-44/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:43:41-44/r13.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:43:41-44/r13.claim: Alternatively, they will be asked about the Qurʾan and their duty to uphold its rights.
TABRISI:43:41-44/r13.anchor: وقيل: تسألون عن القرآن وعما يلزمكم من القيام بحقه

THALABI:v8p335/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p335/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p335/r11.claim: The Quran is an honor for Muhammad and his people, Quraysh, as in 21:10; they will be asked to uphold its rights and give thanks for it.
THALABI:v8p335/r11.anchor: لذكر لك لشرف لك ولقومك من قريش، نظيره قوله: لقد أنزلنا إليكم كتابا فيه ذكركم

THALABI:v8p336/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p336/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v8p336/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says Muhammad presented himself to Meccan tribes and promised victory; when they asked who would rule after him, he withheld an answer until the verse named him and his people, Quraysh. Thereafter he answered “Quraysh,” which they rejected, while the Ansar accepted it.
THALABI:v8p336/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس. قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يعرض نفسه على القبائل بمكة، ويعدهم الظهور

THALABI:v8p336/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p336/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v8p336/r2.claim: Through Ibn Umar, the Prophet says leadership will remain among Quraysh while at least two people remain.
THALABI:v8p336/r2.anchor: عن ابن عمر، إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «لا يزال هذا الأمر في قريش ما بقي من الناس اثنان»

THALABI:v8p336/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p336/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v8p336/r3.claim: Through Muawiya, the Prophet says Quraysh will retain leadership, and whoever opposes them will be cast face-first so long as they uphold the religion.
THALABI:v8p336/r3.anchor: عن معاوية، قال: سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: «لا يزال هذا الأمر في قريش لا يعاديهم أحد إلا كب على وجهه ما أقاموا الدين

THALABI:v8p337/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p337/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v8p337/r1.claim: Through Abu Musa, the Prophet says that a Qurayshi's sister's son counts as one of the people; Quraysh leadership endures when rulers judge justly, show compassion, and keep covenants, while failure brings God's curse and rejection of deeds.
THALABI:v8p337/r1.anchor: «ابن أخت القوم منهم» ثم قال: «لا يزال هذا الأمر في قريش ما داموا إذا حكموا فعدلوا، واسترحموا فرحموا، وعاهدوا فوفوا

THALABI:v8p337/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p337/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v8p337/r2.claim: Through Abu Burda, the Prophet says rulers are from Quraysh and rulers and subjects each have rights as long as rulers judge justly, show compassion, and fulfill covenants; Khalid adds a curse for failure.
THALABI:v8p337/r2.anchor: عن أبي بردة، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «الأمراء من قريش، لي عليهم حق ولهم عليكم حق ما فعلوا ثلاثا

THALABI:v8p337/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p337/r3.speaker: مالك بن أنس
THALABI:v8p337/r3.claim: Malik interprets “a remembrance for you and your people” as the honor of a man saying, “My father told me, from my grandfather.”
THALABI:v8p337/r3.anchor: سمعت مالك بن أنس يقول: في قول الله تعالى: وإنه لذكر لك ولقومك قال: قول الرجل: حدثني أبي، عن جدي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p50/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p50/r1.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p50/r1.claim: The phrase “a remembrance for you” is explained as “an honor for you,” with a comparison to 21:10.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p50/r1.anchor: {لذكر لك} قالوا لشرف لك كقوله: {لقد أنزلنا إليكم كتابا فيه ذكركم}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p50/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p50/r2.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p50/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas and Muqatil take the Prophet's people here to mean those among them who believed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p50/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومقاتل: لمن آمن منهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p50/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p50/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p50/r3.claim: The word “people” may mean everyone to whom the Prophet was sent or specifically Quraysh.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p50/r3.anchor: والقوم يحتمل كل من بعث إليه من الناس، ويحتمل أن يراد به قريش

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p50/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p50/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p50/r4.claim: If the people are believers, the Qur'an honors the Prophet through wisdom and honors them by letting them recognize truth; if Quraysh, it honors them because it was revealed to one of them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p50/r4.anchor: ويكون المعنى على هذا: القرآن شرف لك بما أعطاك الله من الحكمة ولقومك المؤمنين بما عوضهم من إدراك الحق به

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p50/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p50/r5.speaker: ابن عباس (رواية الضحاك)
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p50/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak reports from Ibn Abbas that the Prophet did not answer who would lead after him until this verse descended, then answered “Quraysh.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p50/r5.anchor: وروى الضحاك عن ابن عباس: أن النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- كان إذا سئل لمن هذا الأمر بعدك؟ لم يخبر بشيء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p50/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p50/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p50/r6.claim: The report suggests the Prophet understood the verse to indicate leadership over Muslims through prophethood and honor because the Qur'an came to a Qurayshi man.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p50/r6.anchor: وهذا يدل على أن -صلى الله عليه وسلم- فهم من هذا أنه يلي على المسلمين بحكم النبوة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p50/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p50/r7.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p50/r7.claim: Mujahid explains the honor as a lineage exchange identifying a person first as Arab, then Qurayshi, then from Banu Hashim.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p50/r7.anchor: وقال مجاهد: هو أن يقول الرجل لأخيه: ممن الرجل؟ فيقول: من العرب، فيقول: من أي العرب؟

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p50/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p50/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p50/r8.claim: On Mujahid's reading, the Qur'an honors Muhammad, the Arabs, and especially his closest clan; because the Qur'an honors them and they honor him, it honors everyone.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p50/r8.anchor: هذا والله هو الذكر والشرف، وعلى هذا # القول: القرآن شرف لمحمد وهو شرف للعرب

ZAJJAJ:v4p413/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p413/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p413/r1.claim: The Qur’an is an honor and distinction for Muhammad and his people.
ZAJJAJ:v4p413/r1.anchor: يريد أن القرآن شرف لك ولقومك

ZAJJAJ:v4p413/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p413/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p413/r2.claim: They will be asked whether they were grateful for the honor God granted them.
ZAJJAJ:v4p413/r2.anchor: معناه سوف تسألون عن شكر ما جعله الله لكم من الشرف

ASAD-NOTES:43:43#n36/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:43:43#n36/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:43:43#n36/r1.claim: Asad renders dhikr here as 'a source of eminence'.
ASAD-NOTES:43:43#n36/r1.anchor: For the above rendering of dhikr as "[a source of] eminence", see first half of note 13 on 21:10.

ASAD-NOTES:43:43#n37/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:43:43#n37/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:43:43#n37/r1.claim: On Judgment Day, prophets are metaphorically asked what response their people gave to their message.
ASAD-NOTES:43:43#n37/r1.anchor: The meaning is that on the Day of Judgment all prophets will be asked, metaphorically, as to what response they received from their people

ASAD-NOTES:43:43#n37/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:43:43#n37/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:43:43#n37/r2.claim: Followers will answer for the spiritual and social use they made of revelation; Muhammad's community's promised eminence depends on conduct, not professed faith alone.
ASAD-NOTES:43:43#n37/r2.anchor: those who professed to follow them will be called to account for the spiritual and social use they made

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p199/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p199/r1.speaker: مجاهد
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p199/r1.claim: Mujāhid explains the verse as an honor for the Prophet and his people: people trace his lineage from Arabs to Quraysh and finally Banū Hāshim.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p199/r1.anchor: عن ابن عيينة عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد في قوله تعالى ﴿ وإنه لذكر لك ولقومك ﴾ قال يقال ممن هذا الرجل

ALUSI-FULL:v25p85/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p85/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v25p85/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Suddi, and Ibn Zayd identify the Prophet’s people as Quraysh; the Quran is a great honor for them. Alusi prefers this interpretation.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p85/r1.anchor: هم قريش على ما روي عن ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة والسدي وابن زيد

ALUSI-FULL:v25p85/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p85/r2.speaker: علي وابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v25p85/r2.claim: A report from Ali and Ibn Abbas says the Prophet sought support among Meccan tribes and promised victory; asked who would rule after him, he withheld an answer until this verse, then named Quraysh, who accepted only after the Ansar did. No grading is stated.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p85/r2.anchor: وأخرج ابن عدي وابن مردويه عن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه وابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما قالا

ALUSI-FULL:v25p85/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p85/r3.speaker: عدي بن حاتم
ALUSI-FULL:v25p85/r3.claim: A report from Adi ibn Hatim says God knew the Prophet’s love for his people and gave them glad tidings through this verse, making Quraysh renowned; it also praises Quraysh and mentions the truthful one and martyr among them. No grading is stated.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p85/r3.anchor: قال ألا إن الله تعالى علم ما في قلبي من حبي لقومي فبشرني فيهم

ALUSI-FULL:v25p85/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p85/r4.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v25p85/r4.claim: Another view takes ‘your people’ as all Arabs because the Quran came in their language, with honor concentrated increasingly among closer groups, especially Quraysh and Banu Hashim.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p85/r4.anchor: وقيل هم العرب مطلقا لما أن القرآن نزل بلغتهم ثم يختص بذلك الشرف الأخص فالأخص

ALUSI-FULL:v25p85/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p85/r5.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v25p85/r5.claim: Qatadah is also reported to identify the Prophet’s people as his followers from the Muslim community.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p85/r5.anchor: عن قتادة هم مناتبعه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم من أمته

ALUSI-FULL:v25p85/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p85/r6.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v25p85/r6.claim: Al-Hasan says the people are the Muslim community, making the Quran a reminder for the Prophet and his nation; Alusi favors Quraysh.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p85/r6.anchor: قال الحسن : هم الأمة والمعنى وإنه لتذكرة وموعظة لك ولأمتك

ALUSI-FULL:v25p85/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p85/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p85/r7.claim: On the primary reading, people will be asked on Judgment Day about the Quran and whether they fulfilled its rights.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p85/r7.anchor: يوم القيامة عنه وعن قيامكم بحقوقه

ALUSI-FULL:v25p85/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p85/r8.speaker: الحسن والكلبي والزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v25p85/r8.claim: Al-Hasan, al-Kalbi, and al-Zajjaj instead say people will be asked to thank God for the honor bestowed on them.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p85/r8.anchor: وقال الحسن والكلبي والزجاج : تسئلون عن شكر ما جعله الله تعالى لكم من الشرف

ALUSI-FULL:v25p85/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p85/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p85/r9.claim: The verse indicates that people naturally desire good praise and lasting renown: God presents this honor as a favor, and noble remembrance stands in for continued life.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p85/r9.anchor: قيل إن هذه الآية تدل على أن الإنسان يرغب في الثناء الحسن والذكر الجميل

ALUSI-FULL:v25p85/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p85/r10.speaker: ابن دريد
ALUSI-FULL:v25p85/r10.claim: Ibn Duraid’s verse says a person lives on as a story after death and urges the listener to leave a good account.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p85/r10.anchor: وقال ابن دريد : وإنما المرء حديث بعده

ALUSI-FULL:v25p85#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p85#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p85#2/r1.claim: A following poetic saying calls the world’s finest beauty the good report that remains after a person is gone.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p85#2/r1.anchor: وقال آخر إنما الدنيا محاسنها طيب ما يبقى من الخبر

ALUSI-FULL:v25p85#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p85#2/r2.speaker: هلاكو
ALUSI-FULL:v25p85#2/r2.claim: In an anecdote, Hulagu asks who is king; courtiers praise his conquests, but he points to the Prophet, dead for over six centuries yet named by callers to prayer five times daily, as enduring renown.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p85#2/r2.anchor: ويحكى أن الطاغية هلاكو سأل أصحابه من الملك فقالوا : له أنت الذي دوخت البلاد

DURR-FULL:v7p380/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p380/r1.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p380/r1.claim: Qatāda identifies the reminder as the Qur'an and the Prophet's people as his followers.
DURR-FULL:v7p380/r1.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه {وإنه لذكر لك} يعني القرآن

DURR-FULL:v7p380/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p380/r2.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v7p380/r2.claim: Mujāhid says the verse grants honor: people's Arab, Qurashi, and Hāshimī lineage is publicly identified.
DURR-FULL:v7p380/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله: {وإنه لذكر لك ولقومك}

DURR-FULL:v7p380/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p380/r3.speaker: علي وابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p380/r3.claim: A report says the Prophet withheld an answer when Meccan tribes asked who would rule after him; after the verse he said Quraysh, and the tribes refused until the Anṣār accepted.
DURR-FULL:v7p380/r3.anchor: عن علي وابن عباس قالا: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يعرض نفسه على القبائل بمكة ويعدهم الظهور فإذا قالوا لمن الملك بعدك أمسك

DURR-FULL:v7p380/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p380/r4.speaker: عدي بن حاتم
DURR-FULL:v7p380/r4.claim: ʿAdī reports God honored the Prophet in Quraysh through this verse, which the Prophet often recited with pleasure.
DURR-FULL:v7p380/r4.anchor: عن عدي بن حاتم رضي الله عنه قال: كنت قاعدا عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: ألا إن الله علم ما في قلبي من حبي لقومي فشرفني فيهم

DURR-FULL:v7p380/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p380/r5.speaker: عدي بن حاتم
DURR-FULL:v7p380/r5.claim: ʿAdī links Quraysh's honor to commands to warn close kin and be gentle with believers.
DURR-FULL:v7p380/r5.anchor: عن عدي بن حاتم رضي الله عنه قال: كنت قاعدا عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v7p380/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p380/r6.speaker: عدي بن حاتم
DURR-FULL:v7p380/r6.claim: ʿAdī identifies Quraysh as the blessed tree: its fixed root is noble ancestry and its branches the honor of Islam.
DURR-FULL:v7p380/r6.anchor: عن عدي بن حاتم رضي الله عنه قال: كنت قاعدا عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v7p380/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p380/r7.speaker: عدي بن حاتم
DURR-FULL:v7p380/r7.claim: ʿAdī says God revealed Sūrat Quraysh in Mecca about Quraysh and cites its opening verses.
DURR-FULL:v7p380/r7.anchor: عن عدي بن حاتم رضي الله عنه قال: كنت قاعدا عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3283#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3283#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3283#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Quran is an honor for the Prophet and his people.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3283#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما وانه لذكر لك ولقومك قال : للقران شرف لك ولقومك

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3283#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3283#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3283#2/r2.claim: Mujahid explains the verse as an enduring distinction: when asked about the Prophet’s lineage, people identify him as an Arab, from Quraysh, and from Banu Hashim.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3283#2/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله : وانه لذكر لك ولقومك قال : يقال ممن هذا الرجل ؟ فيقال : من العرب ، فيقال : من اي العرب ؟

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p221/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p221/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p221/r1.claim: The Qur’an is a cause of remembrance because it gives its people honor by which they are remembered.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p221/r1.anchor: القرآن سبب الذكر لأنه يكسب قومه شرفا يذكرون بسببه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p221/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p221/r2.speaker: علي وابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p221/r2.claim: This explanation of dhikr as honor is transmitted from Ali and Ibn Abbas in reports cited by Ibn ʿAdi and Ibn Mardawayh.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p221/r2.anchor: وقد روي هذا التفسير عن علي وابن عباس في رواية ابن عدي وابن مردويه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p221/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p221/r3.speaker: القرطبي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p221/r3.claim: Al-Qurtubi explains that the Qur’an honors the Prophet and Quraysh: it came in Quraysh’s language, needed by people of other languages who believed.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p221/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p221/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p221/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reportedly said that after this verse came down, he answered Quraysh when tribes asked the Prophet who would hold authority after him; al-Kashshaf follows this account.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p221/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عطية ( قال ابن عباس كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يعرض نفسه على القبائل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p221/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p221/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p221/r5.claim: The word dhikr allows the favorable sense of renown; praising the Prophet and his people also indirectly censures those who oppose them.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p221/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p221/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p221/r6.claim: Qawmihi can mean Quraysh, the direct audience, or all Arabs, honored by the Prophet’s people and the Qur’an’s language; this renown has endured, whereas otherwise major peoples would scarcely know the Arabs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p221/r6.anchor: وقومه هم قريش لأنهم المقصود بالكلام أو جميع العرب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p221/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p221/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p221/r7.claim: This is the Qur’an’s seventh commendation in the passage.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p221/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p221/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p221/r8.claim: The question is accountability: believers will be asked how fully they acted on their obligations, while polytheists face rebuke and threat.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p221/r8.anchor: فسؤال المؤمنين عن مقدار العمل بما كلفوا به ، وسؤال المشركين سؤال توبيخ وتهديد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p221/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p221/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p221/r9.claim: The command to ask represents how widely known and certain a report is; al-Samawʾal (or al-Harithī) and Zayd al-Khayl use similar challenges in poetry.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p221/r9.anchor: الأمر بالسؤال هنا تمثيل لشهرة الخبر وتحققه كما في قول السمؤال أو الحارثي :

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p318/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p318/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p318/r1.claim: The Quran is an honor for Muhammad through what God has given him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p318/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى ﴿ وإنه ﴾ يعني القرآن ﴿ لذكر لك ﴾ أي شرف لك بما أعطاك الله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p318/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p318/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p318/r2.claim: Mujahid takes Muhammad's people to mean all Arabs; the Quran honors them because it was revealed in their language.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p318/r2.anchor: ومذهب مجاهد أن القوم هاهنا العرب والقرآن شرف لهم إذ أنزل بلغتهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p318/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p318/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p318/r3.claim: One reported view takes Muhammad's people to mean Quraysh.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p318/r3.anchor: في قومه ثلاثة أقوال أحدها العرب قاطبة والثاني قريش

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p318/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p318/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p318/r4.claim: A third view takes Muhammad's people to mean everyone who believed in him.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p318/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p318/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p318/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak reports from Ibn Abbas that the Prophet answered questions about who would hold authority after him only after this verse was revealed, after which he said Quraysh.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p318/r5.anchor: وقد روى الضحاك عن ابن عباس أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا سئل لمن هذا الأمر من بعدك لم يخبر بشيء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p318/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p318/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p318/r6.claim: Ibn al-Jawzi infers that Muhammad understood the verse to mean he would lead the Muslims by prophethood and that his people would succeed him in authority because the Quran honored one of them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p318/r6.anchor: وهذا يدل على أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فهم من هذا أنه يلي على المسلمين بحكم النبوة وشرف القرآن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p318/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p318/r7.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p318/r7.claim: Ibn Qutayba explains the use of dhikr for honor by saying that a noble person is remembered.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p318/r7.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة إنما وضع الذكر موضع الشرف لأن الشريف يذكر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p318/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p318/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p318/r8.claim: One view says people will be asked to give thanks for the honor they received.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p318/r8.anchor: أحدهما عن شكر ما أعطيتم من ذلك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p318/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p318/r9.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p318/r9.claim: Another view says people will be asked about the obligations attached to this honor.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p318/r9.anchor: والثاني عما لزمكم فيه من الحقوق

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p229/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p229/r1.speaker: قيل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p229/r1.claim: One view takes the Qur'an as an honor for the Prophet's people because it was revealed in their language, which they understand best and should follow most fully; the earliest emigrants exemplified this.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p229/r1.anchor: شرف لهم من حيث إنه أنزل بلغتهم، فهم أفهم الناس له

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p229/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p229/r2.speaker: قيل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p229/r2.claim: Another view understands the verse as a reminder for the Prophet and his people; naming them does not exclude others, as other verses show.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p229/r2.anchor: تخصيصهم بالذكر لا ينفي من سواهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p229/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p229/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p229/r3.claim: People will be questioned about the Qur'an and how they acted on it and responded to its call.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p229/r3.anchor: عن هذا القرآن وكيف كنتم في العمل به والاستجابة له

BURSEVI:v8p287/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p287/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p287/r1.claim: A report promises Paradise to whoever professes God's oneness and Muhammad's messengership, even if sins equal the sea's foam, raindrops, stars, or days of the world.
BURSEVI:v8p287/r1.anchor: إلا الله وأن محمدا رسول الله ، أسكنته الجنة ، ولو كانت ذنوبه مثل زبد البحر ، وعدد القطر

BURSEVI:v8p287/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p287/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p287/r2.claim: The Torah describes this community's scriptures as in their hearts, meaning they memorize their book.
BURSEVI:v8p287/r2.anchor: وفي التوراة في حق هذه الأمة : أناجيلهم في صدورهم ؛ أي : يحفظون كتابهم.

BURSEVI:v8p287/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p287/r3.speaker: المثنوي
BURSEVI:v8p287/r3.claim: The Mathnawi couplets liken the Quran to a human: visible markings show outwardly while its spirit stays hidden; the devil sees Adam only as clay.
BURSEVI:v8p287/r3.anchor:
وفي المثنوي :
تو زقرآن اى بسر ظاهر مبين
ديو آدم رانه بيند جز كه طين

JISHUMI:v1p650/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p650/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p650/r4.claim: Dhikr can also mean honor or renown, as when the Qurʾān is called a remembrance for the Prophet and his people.

MUQATIL:43:44-45/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:43:44-45/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:43:44-45/r1.claim: The Qur’an is an honor for Muhammad and those in his community who believe.
MUQATIL:43:44-45/r1.anchor: يقول: القرآن لشرف لك، { ولقومك } ، ولمن آمن منهم

MUQATIL:43:44-45/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:43:44-45/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:43:44-45/r2.claim: They will be asked in the Hereafter about those who disbelieved in the Qur’an.
MUQATIL:43:44-45/r2.anchor: وسوف تسألون } [آية: 44] في الآخرة عن من يكذب به

NASAFI-FULL:v4p115#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p115#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p115#5/r1.claim: The revelation is an honor for the Prophet and his community.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p115#5/r1.anchor: ﴿ وإنه ﴾ وان الذى أوحى إليك ﴿ لذكر لك ﴾ لشرف لك

NASAFI-FULL:v4p115#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p115#5/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p115#5/r2.claim: At the Resurrection they will be asked whether they fulfilled its rights, honored it, and thanked God for this blessing.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p115#5/r2.anchor: عنه يوم القيامة وعن قيامكم بحقه وعن تعظيمكم له وعن شكركم هذه النعمة

STUDYQURAN:43:44/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:44/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:43:44/r1.claim: Al-dhikr, the Reminder, is one of the Quran’s names.
STUDYQURAN:43:44/r1.anchor: is one of the names of the Quran

STUDYQURAN:43:44/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:44/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:43:44/r2.claim: Reminder can also mean scripture generally or the Torah; the People of the Book are called the people of the Reminder.
STUDYQURAN:43:44/r2.anchor: also employed as a reference to scripture in general or to the Torah

STUDYQURAN:43:44/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:44/r3.speaker: IK, JJ, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:43:44/r3.claim: They understand the Quran as an honor bestowed on the Prophet and his people.
STUDYQURAN:43:44/r3.anchor: the Quran is an honor bestowed upon the Prophet and his people (IK, JJ, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:43:44/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:44/r4.speaker: IK, JJ
STUDYQURAN:43:44/r4.claim: The Quran is an honor to them especially because it was revealed in their own language.
STUDYQURAN:43:44/r4.anchor: especially since it was a revelation sent down in their own language (IK, JJ)

STUDYQURAN:43:44/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:44/r5.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:43:44/r5.claim: Because they can best understand its language, the Prophet’s people should be most steadfast in following it.
STUDYQURAN:43:44/r5.anchor: they should be the most steadfast in adhering to it (IK)

STUDYQURAN:43:44/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:44/r6.speaker: JJ
STUDYQURAN:43:44/r6.claim: They will be questioned in the Hereafter about how fully they fulfilled their duty toward the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:43:44/r6.anchor: they will be questioned in the Hereafter regarding the degree to which they have fulfilled their duty toward it (JJ)

TAB-FULL:v20p602#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p602#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p602#2/r1.claim: The Qur’an is an honor for Muhammad and his Quraysh people.
TAB-FULL:v20p602#2/r1.anchor: عن علي، عن ابن عباس، قوله: {وإنه لذكر لك ولقومك} [الزخرف: 44] يقول: «إن القرآن شرف لك»

TAB-FULL:v20p602#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p602#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p602#2/r2.claim: Allah will ask Muhammad and his people what they did with the Qur’an’s commands and whether they obeyed its prohibitions.
TAB-FULL:v20p602#2/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: {وإنه لذكر لك ولقومك} [الزخرف: 44] قال: " يقول للرجل: من أنت؟ فيقول: من العرب

TAB-FULL:v20p602#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p602#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v20p602#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Qur’an is an honor for the Prophet.
TAB-FULL:v20p602#2/r3.anchor: عن علي، عن ابن عباس، قوله: {وإنه لذكر لك ولقومك} [الزخرف: 44] يقول: «إن القرآن شرف لك»

TAB-FULL:v20p602#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p602#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v20p602#2/r4.claim: Mujāhid illustrates Quraysh’s honor by describing how a man identifies himself first as Arab and then as Qurayshī.
TAB-FULL:v20p602#2/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: {وإنه لذكر لك ولقومك} [الزخرف: 44] قال: " يقول للرجل: من أنت؟ فيقول: من العرب

TAB-FULL:v20p602#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p602#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v20p602#2/r5.claim: Qatāda says the reference is to this Qur’an.
TAB-FULL:v20p602#2/r5.anchor: عن قتادة، {وإنه لذكر لك ولقومك} [الزخرف: 44] «وهو هذا القرآن»

TAB-FULL:v20p602#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p602#2/r6.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v20p602#2/r6.claim: Al-Suddī says the Qur’an is an honor for Muhammad and his people.
TAB-FULL:v20p602#2/r6.anchor: عن السدي، {وإنه لذكر لك ولقومك} [الزخرف: 44] قال: «شرف لك ولقومك، يعني القرآن»

TAB-FULL:v20p602#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p602#2/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v20p602#2/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd asks whether prophethood and the Qur’an revealed to the Prophet were not an honor for him and his people.
TAB-FULL:v20p602#2/r7.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {وإنه لذكر لك ولقومك} [الزخرف: 44] قال: «أولم تكن النبوة والقرآن الذي أنزل على نبيه

TAB-FULL:v1p96/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p96/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p96/r3.claim: Tabari reads “a reminder for you and your people” in 43:44 as honor and renown for the Prophet and his people.
TAB-FULL:v1p96/r3.anchor: يعني به أنه شرف له ولقومه

SULAMI:v2p234#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p234#3/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p234#3/r1.claim: Ibn Ata says the Qur'an honors Muhammad through its relation to God, and honors his people through their relation to him.
SULAMI:v2p234#3/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : شرف لك بانتسابك إلينا وشرف لقومك بالانتساب إليك .

SULAMI:v2p234#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p234#3/r2.speaker: مالك بن أنس
SULAMI:v2p234#3/r2.claim: Malik interprets the verse as the inherited honor expressed by a man saying, 'my father, from my grandfather.'
SULAMI:v2p234#3/r2.anchor: مالك بن أنس في قوله : ﴿ وإنه لذكر لك ولقومك ﴾ قال : هو قول الرجل ابى عن جدي .

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p398/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p398/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p398/r1.claim: The Qur'an is a source of honor and renown for the Prophet and his people.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p398/r1.anchor: وإنه لذكر لك ولقومك} أي شرف لكم؛ يعني القرآن (6) .

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p398/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p398/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p398/r2.claim: They will be asked whether they showed gratitude for the Qur'an.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p51/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p51/r1.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p51/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi says they will be asked whether they gave thanks for the honor bestowed on them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p51/r1.anchor: قال الكلبي: أي عن هذا الشرف هل أديتم شكره

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p51/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p51/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p51/r2.claim: Muqatil takes the question as a rebuke to those who rejected the Quran: why did you reject it?
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p51/r2.anchor: وقال مقاتل: يعني من كذب به، كأن يسأل: لم كذب به؟ (¬2) فيسأل سؤال توبيخ.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p51/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p51/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p51/r3.claim: Abu Ishaq says they will be asked to give thanks for the honor God gave them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p51/r3.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: سوف تسألون عن شكر ما جعله الله لكم من الشرف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p51/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p51/r4.speaker: غيره
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p51/r4.claim: Another view says they will be questioned about the Quran, their obedience to its commands, and their duty to uphold its rights.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p51/r4.anchor: وقال غيره: تسألون عن القرآن وعملكم بما أمرتم به فيه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:44-45/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:44-45/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:44-45/r1.claim: The Quran is an honor for Muhammad and his people because it was revealed to him, in their language, and he is one of them.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:44-45/r1.anchor: وإنه } أي: القرآن { لذكر } لشرف { لك ولقومك } إذ نزل بلغتهم، ونزل عليك وأنت منهم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:44-45/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:44-45/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:44-45/r2.claim: They will be asked to show gratitude for the distinction God gave them.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:44-45/r2.anchor: عن شكر ما جعلنا لكم من الشرف

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p95/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p95/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p95/r4.claim: ذكر can stand for honor because the honored person is remembered; the Quran is a distinction for the Prophet and his people, and ذكركم means your honor.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p95/r4.anchor: ومنه الذكر يوضع موضع الشرف، لأن الشريف يذكر

TABRISI:38:2-5/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:38:2-5/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:38:2-5/r1.claim: A related verse says the Quran is a remembrance for Muhammad and his people.

BAQILLANI:v1p76/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p76/r5.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p76/r5.claim: In “a remembrance for you and your people,” remembrance means something by which they gain honor.
BAQILLANI:v1p76/r5.anchor: يريد ما يكون الذكر عنه شرفا

BAQILLANI:v1p76/r6.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p76/r6.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p76/r6.claim: The Qurʾān frequently uses metaphor, as shown by the “remembrance” phrase and the other cited examples.

BURHAN:v4p280/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p280/r10.speaker: الزمخشري وابن الخشاب وابن يعيش وابن أبان وابن بابشاذ وابن عصفور
BURHAN:v4p280/r10.claim: Zamakhsharī and several grammarians hold that سوف signals a longer delay than sin; the nearby سيقول contrasts with وسوف تسألون.
BURHAN:v4p280/r10.anchor: حرف يدل على التأخير والتنفيس وزمانه ابعد من زمان السين

ITQAN:v2p329#5/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p329#5/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p329#5/r4.claim: The phrase “it is a reminder” uses dhikr in the sense of honor.
